frames.title: Who is up: the heights they wait for

notes.text: **The clockwork.** Dividers cut the sixteenths into eighths, dotted eighths, bars and phrases. Two gears, five bars and seven, meet every 35: an **eclipse**, a gong, and the Twins pulled back into step. The song is 140 bars, so it begins and ends on one.

**No score: orbits.** The **Day** climbs for 200 s and sets in 100. Each voice waits for a height of it (the Logic thresholds below) and leaves, in turn, as it sets. The **Tide**, 80 bars round, takes the bass and drums away once and brings them back. **Moon A** and **B**, seven and five notes long, drift against the dotted eighths that sample them: that's the melody. The Day's rate is a Quantizer holding a voltage, and the **Sundial** tells it when to set.

**The Twins** play one two-bar figure in sixteen and fifteen eighths: one keeps the bar, the other slips an eighth a pass. A heartbeat kick sets the bar before the cross-rhythms arrive. **The Moon** sings what the orbits say, as wide as the Day is high: two notes at dawn, a sweep at noon, and silence when its range closes. **The Comet** samples the same orbits slower, and only near noon. Open a group to see inside it.
